Stimulus protocol

PYTHON

Write a sequence, then run it on the rig. image(filename, ...) presents an uploaded or sample image; blank(duration) inserts a gray interval. Durations are seconds.

Present an image
image("my_image.png", duration=1, x=0, y=0, size=0.6, rotation=0)

Use an exact filename from the image library. Upload PNG, JPEG or WebP images. blank(duration=0.5) inserts a gray interval. Durations are seconds.

Position and size: x spans −1.5…1.5; y spans −1…1, positive downward. Size is the longest side of the image in screen half-height units; size 1 fills half the screen height. Aspect ratio is preserved.

Rotation: rotation is clockwise degrees around the image center. 0 keeps its original orientation. For example:

for angle in range(0, 360, 30):
    blank(duration=0.5)
    image("my_curve.png", duration=1,
          x=0, y=0, size=0.8, rotation=angle)

Replace my_curve.png with your uploaded filename. Combine images, positions, sizes and rotations using Python loops, lists, math, and random. The code builds a sequence before presentation. Maximum: 300 seconds / 1,000 segments. Image name, position, size and rotation are saved with each presentation.

One simulated neuron.

Explore: what makes the neuron fire?

Imagine an electrode is recording from a visual neuron. You can see its spikes in the voltage trace and hear them as clicks. Find a stimulus that makes the neuron respond strongly.

  • Start the webcam and turn on sound. Draw a black bar on white paper and hold it in front of the camera.
  • Explore position. Move the bar around the image and look for a sensitive region.
  • Explore orientation. Rotate the bar and listen for changes in the response.
  • Try different bar widths, lengths and movements. Keep other features steady so you can tell what matters.

Does the neuron respond everywhere? Which angle works best? Can you find a strong stimulus and a weak one?

Goal: figure out what makes this neuron fire.
